solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A fellow admitting misdemeanour finally can't somehow function

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the opening pair of words takes the other letters inside them

parts.note: a gent is a fellow, a man

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word misdemeanour
somehow says the letters of can't are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A man who owns up to a minor offence somehow can't keep working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges CANT to CTAN; the apostrophe in 'can't' is ignored, as punctuation always is.
explanation.definitionFit: The arc tangent is a trigonometric function, the inverse of the tangent.

clue.text: Quick-moving river into which doctor falls

indicators.note: into which says something goes inside the river just named
falls completes the picture of the doctor dropping into the water

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A fast-flowing river claims a doctor who tumbles in.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimble describes someone light and quick on their feet, a synonym for agile.

clue.text: One moving things around managed party, not a generous type

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it; past tense ran
a do is a party or celebration
a miser hoards money rather than giving it

explanation.surface: A mean host ran a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A randomiser shuffles or mixes items into an unpredictable order, as in a lottery machine.

clue.text: Capital that is very minimal after end of bank

indicators.note: after says the other pieces follow that letter
end of picks out the closing letter of the word bank

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is
very cut to a minimum is its abbreviation V

explanation.surface: A financial capital whose bank holdings are tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiev, now often spelt Kyiv, is the capital city of Ukraine.

clue.text: Call to embrace friend doing well after illness?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the call wraps round the friend

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A phone call to hug a friend who is getting better.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient rallying is recovering strength, regaining health after a setback.

clue.text: Place at which musicians may stop being excellent

definitions.text: Place at which musicians may stop
definitions.meaning: the Italian word marked on a score where the piece ends, often after a repeat

explanation.definitionFit: Fine marks the end point in sheet music; fine also means of high quality.

clue.text: Belt up in school period

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the school abbreviation
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tan someone is to thrash or belt them

explanation.surface: A command to be quiet during a school lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the belt word round. 'Belt up' is British slang for 'shut up', which disguises the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is a brief spell or short burst of time, as in sleeping in snatches.

clue.text: I'm ignorant — alas, I will suffer process of being edged out

indicators.note: the words will suffer so that their letters are knocked into a new shape

explanation.surface: An ignorant speaker laments that they will suffer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marginalisation pushes a person or group to the fringes of society, away from the centre.

clue.text: Shock the wife, providing man's book

parts.note: a shock of hair is a thick mass, as is a mat of hair
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogy

explanation.surface: Giving the wife a fright, provided some man reads a book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gospel of Matthew is a book of the New Testament named after a man.

clue.text: I disapprove of that teacher putting men off

indicators.note: putting off means the men are taken away from the teacher

parts.note: a tutor is a private teacher
OR, other ranks, means soldiers or men who are not officers

explanation.surface: A teacher's disapproval puts the men off.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation tut is the clicking sound of disapproval, a reproach.

clue.text: Torment of daughter meeting immoral chaps in risky venture

indicators.note: in places the family members and chaps inside the gamble

parts.note: a bet is a wager, a risky venture
evil means wicked, immoral
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A daughter's anguish after meeting bad men on a reckless gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedevilment is a state of being plagued or harassed, as if by devils.

clue.text: Complainer not taking sides — stamp on that?

indicators.note: sides are the outer edges, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a whinger is a moaner, a persistent complainer

explanation.surface: Someone who grumbles while staying neutral wants to stamp on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stamp on that' sounds like crushing something; a stamp collector mounts a stamp on a small gummed paper hinge.
explanation.definitionFit: Philatelists fix stamps into albums with a stamp hinge, a folded strip of gummed paper.

clue.text: Powerful woman in demonstration about endless suffering

indicators.note: about means the demonstration goes round the other piece

parts.note: a march is a protest demonstration

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trial is an ordeal, a source of suffering

explanation.surface: A strong woman leads a protest march about ongoing hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powerful woman in' looks like a container hint, but 'in' is only a link; 'about' does the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is the female head of a family or clan who holds the authority.

clue.text: What could make one bloated — the awfully cheap meal?

definitions.note: a set menu at a fixed price, usually cheaper than ordering dishes separately

indicators.note: awfully means the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheap meal that leaves the diner feeling awfully bloated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What could make one' introduces the anagram: these letters could make the answer, and a big meal could make you bloated.
explanation.definitionFit: A set menu of several courses at a fixed price, often a cheaper option than ordering à la carte.

clue.text: Labourer making tours, by implication?

indicators.note: making here means the five letters shown are what the jumbled first part produces, so they must be rearranged

parts.note: the word about, a stock signal for rearranging, is implied rather than printed, and it forms the second half

explanation.surface: A worker who goes on tours, it is implied.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as ROUST ABOUT: 'about' is an anagram signal, so ROUST about makes TOURS, which is what the clue implies.
explanation.definitionFit: A roustabout is a casual manual worker, on an oil rig, a dock or with a circus.

clue.text: Tiny birds? They make one cry

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny
pie is an old word for the magpie

explanation.surface: Little birds are a tearjerker.
explanation.definitionFit: Weepies are sentimental films or books meant to bring on tears.

clue.text: One new store that City's invested in is unproductive

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: invested in means one piece is put inside another, as money goes into a fund

parts.note: a fund is a store or reserve
EC, the City of London's postcode, is

explanation.surface: A new shop that a City firm has put money into turns out to make no profit.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district; its postcode area EC makes it a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Infecund means infertile, barren, not productive of offspring or fruit.

clue.text: Comfortable overseas territory to the west for important people

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading right to left

parts.note: snug means cosy, comfortable
Gib, short for Gibraltar, is a British overseas territory

explanation.surface: A cosy British territory lies out to the west.
explanation.definitionFit: Big guns are influential, powerful figures in an organisation or field.

clue.text: PC perhaps always in black

indicators.note: in places the word for always inside the black

parts.note: sable is the heraldic and poetic word for black
ay, also spelt aye, is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A police constable perhaps always dressed in black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' looks like a police constable or a computer; here it is politically correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A politically correct remark is one acceptable to utter, fit to be voiced in polite company.

clue.text: Away from home, frequently regret being improperly adjusted

parts.note: out means not at home
oft is an old word for often, frequently
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone away from home often regrets having a poorly tuned instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of true is out of alignment, not straight or level.

clue.text: Think about having no wingers — OK in football?

indicators.note: wingers play on the flanks, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: to consider something is to think about it

explanation.surface: Pondering a football team with no wide players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wingers' plays on football, where they are the players out wide.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is onside when in a legal position, not caught offside, so the play is allowed.

clue.text: Unpleasant smell at the front of your old cottage

indicators.note: at the front of says the smell comes first

parts.note: BO is body odour
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: A bad smell greets you at the front of your former cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: A bothy is a basic hut in Scotland, often a walkers' shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bothy is a small, simple hut or shelter, often in the Scottish hills, a kind of rustic dwelling.

clue.text: Addition to female attire creates stir

definitions.meaning: a pad or frame worn under a skirt to puff it out at the back

explanation.surface: A new piece of women's fashion causes a sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustle is a Victorian padded frame under a dress; bustle also means busy commotion.

clue.text: Wash cos and cole out — you may find snails

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A gardener washing lettuce and cabbage may come across snails.
explanation.walkthrough: Cos is a lettuce and cole a cabbage, so the surface is a vegetable patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails are proverbially slow, so slow movers are figuratively snails.

clue.text: Having lost head, rings to offer apology

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: hoops are rings

explanation.surface: Having lost one's temper, one phones to say sorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Oops is a quick exclamation said when you make a mistake, a mild sorry.

clue.text: Half left to go up took off

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom
half means only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: departed means left

explanation.surface: Half the party left, getting up and taking off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' keeps DEPA of DEPARTED, and 'to go up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off someone is to mimic them, which is to imitate or ape.

clue.text: Fish in dock

definitions.meaning: to fish with a float or lure
to cut short, as a tail or hair

explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to cut hair short; bob also means to dip for something, as fishing.

clue.text: Words of subordination

parts.note: reads like servile language, but in grammar a subordinate clause cannot stand alone

explanation.definitionFit: A subordinate clause depends on a main clause, so grammarians call it dependent.
